To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the state is still necessary because blockchain-based decentralized governance does not replace the state, but rather complements it.

the State is still necessary for the governance of blockchain-based distributed platforms, because it is the only institution capable to manage the complexity of a decentralized society and to ensure a fair distribution of power in a global context.
blockchain and decentralized platforms are not political tools, but they can be used for political purposes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: what is the role of the state in decentralized governance? Can the blockchain be a substitute for state authority? Can the blockchain replace the state as a central point of coordination? Can the blockchain provide a more democratic alternative than the state?

the following questions: (1) What are the main characteristics of the blockchain and its applications to governance?; (2) How does the blockchain challenge the traditional mechanisms of state authority, citizenship and governance?; (3) What is the role of the state in a decentralized society?; (4) What are the risks of a dominant position of decentralized platforms in the global society?; and (5) How can blockchain technology be regulated in order to preserve the role of the democratic state
the following question: is the State still necessary in a decentralized society?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

blockchain-based decentralized governance is a disruptive technology, which is not a substitute for the State, but a new way of managing interactions within society, which can be considered as complementary to State institutions, provided the right regulatory framework is put in place.
blockchain and decentralized governance are not a threat to the State, but rather an opportunity to improve its efficiency, effectiveness and accountability.
, while the State is not necessary, it is not dispensable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the blockchain is a powerful technology, but it is not a political theory.
the State is still necessary, but its role has to be redefined.
, although blockchain technology is capable to manage social and economic interactions in a decentralized way, the State remains necessary to coordinate social and political interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
blockchain and decentralized governance are not an alternative to the State, but rather a tool to be used by the State to improve efficiency and transparency of public institutions.
a decentralized system is only as democratic as the citizens who participate in it.
the State remains the only political institution able to provide the necessary conditions to the development of a decentralized society.
